about: Substantive corrections shown on the public corrections page, newest first. Record only changes that actually shipped, with the date they were made.

entries.title: Lantern festival dates added; two out-of-date pages withdrawn
entries.summary: The Seoul Tourism Organization has published the 2026 Seoul Lantern Festival dates, so the lantern guide now gives them. Two pages that no longer helped a visitor were withdrawn rather than left online.
changes: Seoul lantern festivals guide: the 2026 Seoul Lantern Festival runs from December 11, 2026 to January 31, 2027, 18:00–23:00. An FAQ page the festival site removed is now cited through its Internet Archive copy.
First Seoul culture day guide withdrawn: it was built around the 2026 Seoul International Garden Show, which has closed. Its address now leads to the three-day culture plan.
Gwangalli M Drone Light Show page withdrawn: it covered a Busan event outside this site's Seoul focus, and its October schedule had gone out of date.
K-drama locations guide: a Visit Seoul article that was taken down was replaced with the Korea Tourism Organization's VisitKorea guide to KPop Demon Hunters locations.

entries.title: Seoul Museum of History Friday closing time
entries.summary: The rainy-day guide said the Seoul Museum of History stays open until 22:00 on Fridays. The museum moved its Friday closing to 21:00 on April 12, 2024; its English visitor page still shows the older time.
changes: Rain, cold or heat guide: Seoul Museum of History Friday hours corrected to 09:00–21:00.

entries.title: Time-limited facts moved into dated notices
entries.summary: Temporary changes such as the October 29 to November 15, 2026 free palace entry, gallery closures and seasonal program end dates now appear as dated notices at the top of the guides they affect and disappear after their end date.
changes: Korean tea culture: the Okin-dong house at Namsangol, where the village holds its tea classes, is a replica of a 1910s house, not a relocated one.

entries.title: Fact-check of 24 culture guides against official sources
entries.summary: We re-read the official page behind every hour, fee, closing day, booking rule, station exit and date in 24 guides. Statements that were wrong or out of date were corrected, claims without an official source were removed, and weaker secondary sources such as Wikipedia and news aggregators were replaced with official pages or the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture.
changes: Five palaces compared: Gyeonghuigung is about eight minutes on foot from Seodaemun Station Exit 4, not six, per the Seoul Museum of History.
Seoul subway and T-money: Owl night buses start at about 23:00, not 23:10, and the single-journey ticket is a contactless card, not a paper ticket.
Bukchon: the Bukchon Traditional Culture Center closes on Mondays and opens Tuesday to Friday 9:00 to 18:00 (Wednesdays to 20:00) and weekends 9:00 to 17:00.
Namsangol Hanok Village: four of the five houses were moved from around Seoul; the Okin-dong house is a replica. Kim Chun-yeong held the rank of owijang, not ojang.
Insadong: King Sejo dedicated the temple Wongaksa in 1465; its ten-story pagoda was completed in 1467.
Jjimjilbang etiquette: the 22:00 to 05:00 rule for under-19s applies to 24-hour venues and lifts when a parent or guardian comes along or consents in writing.

Korean tea culture: the history section is now sourced to the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture; unsupported claims were removed, and Dasinjeon is described as Choui's copy of a Chinese tea text rather than his own work.
Korean holidays: Changdeokgung and Changgyeonggung were also free over Seollal 2026, and six of the ten long weekends in 2027 are Saturday-to-Monday breaks.
